- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce forecast for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates, especially in first 3–5 days; increase early forecast slightly to compensate.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00 followed by 0.33), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 15–30% on forecasted values.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5x historical mean, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts near end of period (last 5–7 days) — especially if sentiment is neutral or declining — apply downward tapering (e.g., linear decay from 1.2x to 0.8x).
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1.00 → 0.33 transitions, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecasted values.
